articles.headline: BofA Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast Into 2027
articles.source: TheStreet (citing Bloomberg report of BofA note)
articles.summary: Bank of America Global Research now expects the Federal Reserve to remain on hold for the rest of 2026, shifting its forecast to two quarter-point cuts in July and September 2027. BofA head of U.S. economics Aditya Bhave stated on May 8 that 'the data simply don't warrant cuts this year,' citing core PCE inflation at 3.2% year-over-year and a stronger-than-expected April jobs report of 115,000 nonfarm payrolls added. The Fed held the benchmark federal funds rate steady at 3.50%–3.75% at its April 29 meeting in an unusually divisive 8–4 vote, the closest since 1992. Goldman Sachs separately projects its first rate cut for December 2026, while traders on the CME FedWatch Tool are pricing the next cut for mid-to-late 2027.

articles.headline: Global Net Lease To Acquire Modiv Industrial REIT In $535M Deal
articles.summary: Global Net Lease (NYSE: GNL) announced a $535 million all-stock merger agreement to acquire Modiv Industrial (NYSE: MDV), the only publicly traded REIT exclusively focused on single-tenant industrial manufacturing real estate. Modiv shareholders will receive 1.975 newly issued GNL shares per Modiv share, representing a 17% premium to Modiv's May 1, 2026 closing price of $18.82 per share. Upon closing—expected in Q3 2026 pending Modiv shareholder approval—existing GNL stockholders will own 89% of the combined company. GNL intends to repay Modiv's balance sheet debt and preferred stock using its revolving credit facility and cash on hand; the deal is expected to be immediately 4% accretive to GNL's AFFO per share.

articles.headline: EQT To Spend $1.1B Buying Into Americold Warehouses
articles.summary: Americold Realty Trust (NYSE: COLD) and EQT's Active Core Infrastructure fund announced a $1.3 billion joint venture covering 12 cold storage facilities across the United States, totaling approximately 124 million cubic feet of temperature-controlled capacity and over 400,000 pallet positions. EQT will acquire a 70% interest in the joint venture while Americold retains a 30% equity stake and continues as day-to-day manager; Americold expects to receive approximately $1.1 billion in net cash proceeds to repay outstanding debt. The transaction is expected to close in Q3 2026 subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. Americold's stock jumped 17% on the announcement; the company had seen its stock fall nearly 70% since 2021 amid oversupply in the cold storage sector.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Industrial Slump Deepens, But Brokers Say Rebound May Be Near
articles.summary: The Inland Empire industrial vacancy rate reached 7.8% in Q1 2026, with negative net absorption of 4.7 million square feet driven by four spaces of 1 million square feet or more that went vacant in the quarter, according to CBRE. Total inventory in the market stands at 660.4 million square feet, with an 8.1% vacancy rate leaving approximately 53.6 million square feet of empty space, per Colliers. New construction deliveries dropped sharply to just 102,000 square feet in Q1 2026, down from nearly 2 million square feet in the same period a year prior. Colliers tracked average asking rents in the Inland Empire West at $1.10 per square foot and IE East at $0.90 per square foot, for a marketwide average of $1.00 per square foot.

articles.headline: Anaheim Industrial Outdoor Storage Site Secures Bridge Loan
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in bridge financing for a 7.75-acre industrial outdoor storage facility at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim, California, on behalf of borrower North Palisade Partners. The non-recourse, three-year, floating-rate loan covers a Class A property totaling 337,590 square feet at the southwest corner of North Jefferson St. and Orangethorpe Ave. The site is fully leased to a Fortune 100 logistics company that uses the facility as secured parking to support two nearby distribution centers, with 161 trailer parking stalls and two points of ingress and egress. The property is located 1.1 miles from State Route 91 and approximately 33 miles from both the Port of Long Beach and Port of Los Angeles. JLL's team was led by Senior Director Peter Thompson, Associate Kyle White, and Analyst Nick Englhard.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Manufacturing Building Sells to Investor
articles.summary: Proficio Realty LLC acquired a 17,767-square-foot industrial manufacturing building at 255 Glider Circle in Corona, California from Mark J. & Ronda L. Haupert for $5.3 million, or $298 per square foot. The single-story reinforced concrete property, built in 1999, currently houses Elastomer Technologies as its tenant. The transaction was reported by CoStar on May 11, 2026. Full details of the transaction terms are available exclusively to CoStar subscribers.

articles.headline: Top Industrial Leases Recognized for Inland Empire — Q1 2026 CoStar Power Broker Awards
articles.summary: CoStar recognized the top Q1 2026 industrial leases in the Inland Empire market, with prominent deals signed by Tireco, Medline, and Unis negotiated by top dealmakers from CBRE. The CoStar Power Broker Awards evaluate all deals that closed during the previous quarter through CoStar's professional research team. Full details of individual lease sizes, terms, and locations are available exclusively to CoStar subscribers.

articles.headline: Columbia Container Lines Inks 68-Month, $13.6M Lease in Fullerton
articles.summary: The Klabin Company/CORFAC International represented Columbia Container Lines LAX, Inc. in a 68-month lease transaction for a 156,096-square-foot industrial property located at 691-701 Burning Tree Rd. in Fullerton, Orange County. The lease is valued at more than $13.6 million. Tyler Rollema, SIOR, and Matt Stringfellow, SIOR, of The Klabin Company represented Columbia Container Lines, which is relocating and expanding from its prior location. No landlord representative was identified in the public report.

articles.headline: Southern California Landlords Hit With Biggest U.S. Industrial Leasing Drop
articles.summary: Industrial landlords in Southern California's Inland Empire posted one of the steepest quarterly occupancy losses of any U.S. industrial market, with tenants vacating 4 million more square feet than they moved into in Q2 2025, per CoStar data. The Inland Empire's vacancy rate reached a 15-year high of 8.5%, prompting landlords to offer rent concessions, lean into renewals, and market top-tier properties. Nationally, industrial tenants vacated more space than they moved into for the first time in 15 years, pushing the U.S. industrial vacancy rate to 7.5%, its highest level in more than a decade. IDC Logistics recently signed two major leases totaling more than 1.1 million square feet in the Inland Empire, and Dedeaux Properties secured a full-building lease in Fontana with global third-party logistics firm Pilot Air Freight.

articles.headline: FOMC Holds Federal Funds Rate at 3.50%–3.75% in Divisive April Vote
articles.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.5% to 3.75% at its April 29, 2026 meeting, marking the third consecutive meeting at which rates were held unchanged. The 8–4 vote was the most divisive FOMC decision since October 1992, with Governor Miran voting to lower rates by 25 basis points and three other members objecting to language in the statement suggesting the Fed would eventually resume cutting rates. The Committee stated it is 'strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.' Kevin Warsh, President Trump's nominated successor to Chair Jerome Powell, was set for a Senate confirmation appointment on May 15.

articles.headline: US Treasuries Hold Losses After Core CPI Tops Estimates on Inflation Worries
articles.summary: U.S. Treasury yields rose two to three basis points across maturities on May 12 after the April Consumer Price Index came in hotter than expected, with 30-year yields hovering around 5%. Interest-rate swaps traders priced in approximately 70% odds of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate increase by April 2027. The April CPI report showed headline inflation at 3.8% year-over-year, above the 3.7% forecast and up from 3.3% in March, driven heavily by energy prices. Stock market futures declined following the release.

articles.headline: CPI Inflation April 2026: Prices Rose 3.8% Annually
articles.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on May 12 that the Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in April on a seasonally adjusted basis, pushing the annual rate to 3.8% — the highest since May 2023 and above the 3.7% consensus forecast. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, increased 0.4% for the month and 2.8% year-over-year, with the monthly rate the highest since January 2025. Energy prices jumped 3.8% for the month, accounting for more than 40% of the headline gain, with gasoline up 28.4% annually. Traders raised odds of a Fed rate hike by year-end to approximately 30%, according to CME Group data.

articles.headline: He's on a Mission to Find Opportunities in Southern California's Choppy Industrial Market
articles.summary: CoStar profiled Lincoln Property investor Sean Perrier, who is pursuing value-add industrial acquisitions in Southern California's Inland Empire, where the firm already owns a cluster of roughly 10 buildings near Ontario ranging from 50,000 to 250,000 square feet. In Los Angeles, occupancy slipped again in Q1 2026, pushing vacancy to 6.6% as asking rents moved lower amid added supply, per CoStar data. The Inland Empire's vacancy stands at 9%, above the national average of 7.5%, with demand turning positive but leverage remaining with tenants. Perrier noted that the bid-ask spread between buyers and sellers remains an obstacle to deal execution.

articles.headline: Global Net Lease Agrees to Pay $535 Million for Modiv Industrial
articles.summary: Global Net Lease, a New York-based industrial-focused REIT, agreed to acquire Modiv Industrial in an all-stock transaction valued at $535 million, pending Modiv shareholder approval and expected to close by September 2026. Modiv owns 42 properties across 14 states with a majority in California, collected $39.1 million in annual base rent in 2025, and describes its portfolio as mission-critical industrial properties supporting U.S. supply chains. The national industrial vacancy rate stands at 7.6% per CoStar data and is expected to peak at 7.8% by year-end 2026. Modiv CEO Aaron Halfacre stated the company believed its portfolio was historically mispriced by the marketplace.

articles.headline: JLL Arranges $26M Bridge Financing for Anaheim Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in bridge financing for a 7.75-acre Class A industrial outdoor storage facility at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim, Orange County. Senior Director Peter Thompson, Associate Kyle White, and Analyst Nick Englhard worked on behalf of borrower North Palisade Partners to secure a non-recourse, three-year, floating-rate loan. The property spans approximately 337,590 square feet. Full loan terms and lender identity were not disclosed.

articles.headline: Hot CPI Report Likely to Put Fed on Guard for Longer-Lasting Inflation; Rate Hike Odds Rising
articles.summary: The April 2026 CPI report showed headline inflation at 3.8% year-over-year, topping the 3.7% forecast, with energy price increases compounding existing tariff-driven inflation pressures. CME FedWatch markets priced in a nearly 98% chance the Fed holds rates steady at its next June meeting, but a nearly 30% chance of a rate hike by December 2026. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack cited this as the fourth major shock in five years following the pandemic, Russia-Ukraine war, and tariffs. Morningstar chief U.S. economist Preston Caldwell noted that odds of a rate hike in 2026, while still below 50%, are rising.

articles.headline: Markets Raise Chances for a Fed Rate Hike Following Hot Inflation Report
articles.summary: Following the April CPI report, traders moved away from expecting Federal Reserve interest rate cuts and began pricing in a better than 1-in-3 chance of a rate hike by year-end, per CME Group's FedWatch tracker. Market pricing removed virtually any chance of a cut through the end of 2027. Jefferies economist Thomas Simons said the Fed is expected to stay on hold as it watches events unfold. Moody's Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi said the deciding factor will be whether inflation expectations continue to move higher.

articles.headline: Goodman Launches Leasing at 1.6M-SF Inland Empire West Logistics Campus in Rancho Cucamonga
articles.summary: Goodman announced it is now leasing Goodman Logistics Center Rancho Cucamonga, described as the largest contiguous logistics campus currently available in the Inland Empire West. The 1.6 million-square-foot campus is now being actively marketed for lease. No lease terms, asking rents, or leasing brokers were disclosed in the announcement. The project represents one of the largest available blocks of logistics space in the Western Inland Empire submarket.

articles.headline: CoStar: U.S. Industrial Vacancy to Rise Into Early 2027, National Rate Remains in Mid-7% Range
articles.summary: CoStar revised its industrial vacancy forecast, projecting the national industrial vacancy rate to remain in the mid-7% range entering Q2 2026 and edge higher into 2027 before beginning a gradual descent. West Coast port markets, including Southern California, are expected to continue underperforming due to reduced demand, with availability in large newer logistics properties near major West Coast ports exceeding 13%. U.S. retail vacancy is separately projected to peak in the mid-4.4% range, edging slightly higher in 2026 before stabilizing. CoStar forecasts increasing industrial demand in the second half of 2026 as the supply overhang begins to absorb.

articles.headline: Port of Long Beach Sets 2025 Record at 9.9M TEUs, Plans $3.2B in Infrastructure Ahead of 2026
articles.summary: The Port of Long Beach concluded 2025 handling a record 9.9 million TEUs — its busiest year in its 115-year history — securing a 48.9% cargo share among San Pedro Bay ports. Newly appointed CEO Dr. Noel Hacegaba projected another 9 million TEU year in 2026, targeting a top-five year by cargo volume. The port announced $3.2 billion in infrastructure investments to double capacity by 2050, including the $1.8 billion Pier B On-Dock Rail Support Facility scheduled for completion in 2032. Hacegaba noted tariffs have reshaped trade patterns, with China's share of cargo declining from 70% to 60% over six years as Southeast Asian countries gained share.

articles.headline: US April Inflation Rises 3.8% as Gasoline Prices Climb on Iran War
articles.summary: The U.S. Consumer Price Index rose 3.8% year-over-year in April 2026, the highest reading since 2023, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data released Tuesday. The increase was driven primarily by surging gasoline prices tied to the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, rose 2.8% annually and 0.4% month-over-month, both above economist estimates. After adjusting for inflation, wages fell for the first time in three years.

articles.headline: 10-Year Treasury Yields Top 4.48% as Yardeni Maintains Calm Outlook
articles.summary: Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research, told Bloomberg Television on Tuesday that he views 10-year Treasury yields between 4.25% and 4.75% as normal and is not alarmed by recent moves. Yardeni had previously raised his year-end S&P 500 target to 8,250 from 7,700, representing 11.5% upside from recent closes. He noted the U.S. bond continues to be viewed globally as a safe haven despite elevated inflation and geopolitical risks.

articles.headline: US CPI Report April 2026: Key Takeaways on Inflation, Consumer Price Index
articles.summary: Bloomberg published a detailed key-takeaways piece on the April 2026 CPI report, covering record-low consumer sentiment, the Iran war's impact on energy prices, and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. The April CPI reading of 3.8% topped the 3.7% Dow Jones consensus estimate. Airline fares surged 20.7% over the past 12 months and beef prices jumped 14.8% year-over-year, while food overall rose 3.2% annually.

articles.headline: S&P 500 Slips 0.16%, Nasdaq Drops 0.71% as Inflation Data, Oil Prices Weigh on Tech
articles.summary: U.S. stocks pulled back on May 12 after a hotter-than-expected April CPI reading and surging oil prices dampened investor sentiment. The S&P 500 closed at 7,400.96 (-0.16%) and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.71% to 26,088.20, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 56.09 points (+0.11%). West Texas Intermediate crude futures jumped 4.19% to settle at $102.18 per barrel. Chip stocks including Qualcomm (-13%), Intel (-8%), and Micron (-3.6%) led the technology sector decline.

articles.headline: April Producer Price Index Scheduled for Release May 13, 2026
articles.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics is releasing the April 2026 Producer Price Index on Wednesday, May 13 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Economists polled by Dow Jones anticipated a headline monthly increase of 0.5%, in line with March's rate, while core PPI excluding food and energy was expected to rise 0.4%. The March PPI showed final demand up 4.0% year-over-year, the largest 12-month advance since February 2023, driven by a 1.6% monthly surge in goods prices.

articles.headline: Brent Crude Holds Near $107/Barrel as Strait of Hormuz Disruptions Persist
articles.summary: Brent crude futures held around $107 per barrel on May 13 after three straight sessions of gains, as the prolonged U.S.-Iran conflict and near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz continued to tighten global energy supplies. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser warned the market is losing roughly 100 million barrels of supply each week and said prolonged disruptions could delay market normalization until next year. The Strait of Hormuz continues to face restrictions from both U.S. and Iranian forces, disrupting flows of crude, LNG, and fuels. WTI crude rose to $101.87 per barrel on May 12, up nearly 60% year-over-year.

articles.headline: Commercial Real Estate Lending Optimism Fades as Caution Takes Hold
articles.summary: Banks have largely paused changes to commercial real estate credit standards, but loan demand has cooled across several CRE categories, according to the Federal Reserve's latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey. In January, banks expected demand to strengthen through 2026, pointing to projected interest rate declines as a key driver, but by April that outlook had softened significantly. The renewed Middle East conflict pushed oil prices to their sharpest increase in four years, reinforcing policymakers' caution about easing monetary policy. The Strait of Hormuz, critical to global oil trade, has been effectively blocked since late February.

articles.headline: Los Angeles 'Mansion Tax' Delivers First Affordable Housing Project
articles.summary: CoStar reported that Los Angeles's Measure ULA transfer tax — the so-called 'mansion tax' — has delivered its first affordable housing project funded by the levy. Measure ULA applies a 4% tax on property sales above $5.3 million and 5.5% on sales above $10.6 million, and has generated approximately $1 billion across more than 1,400 transactions since taking effect in April 2023. Critics point to UCLA and RAND research estimating the policy has resulted in 1,900 fewer apartment units delivered annually, with overall construction permits in Los Angeles falling 40%. The City Council is advancing proposed amendments with a 15-year development exemption for voter consideration in November 2026.

articles.headline: AI Expected to Boost Demand for US Industrial, Office, Retail Space by 12% in Next Decade
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence adoption will boost U.S. property demand for industrial, office, and retail space by approximately 12% over the next decade, adding about 330 million square feet, according to Cushman & Wakefield's baseline scenario forecast reported by CoStar. The report counters widespread fears that AI would reduce the need for commercial real estate, predicting instead that productivity gains from AI will generate net new demand. The forecast represents Cushman & Wakefield's baseline scenario, with upside scenarios projecting even greater demand growth.

articles.headline: Buc-ee's Accelerates Expansion With Locations In 6 More States
articles.summary: Texas-based travel plaza chain Buc-ee's is set to open in six new states — Arizona, Arkansas, Wisconsin, Louisiana, Kansas, and North Carolina — by the end of 2027, extending its footprint from 12 to 20 states. Arizona and Arkansas will receive their first Buc-ee's locations in 2026, with 74,000 SF stores featuring 120 fuel pumps planned for Goodyear, Arizona (June) and Benton, Arkansas (August). The chain currently operates 55 locations and plans travel centers of at least 70,000 SF in each new market. The 37th Texas location is set to open in San Marcos in July.

articles.headline: CBRE Hires Former EQ Office CEO For Property Management Role
articles.summary: CBRE has expanded its asset management capabilities within its U.S. Property Management business by hiring Lisa Picard, former CEO of EQ Office (a Blackstone company), as a Senior Advisor. The firm also hired Chris Doman to lead U.S. asset management services within the Property Management division; Doman previously founded and ran two companies providing asset management and redevelopment services for institutions and family offices. CBRE said the hires are in response to growing client demand for asset management services across various property types.

articles.headline: Hudson Pacific Office Leasing Looking Up, But Big Loan Maturity Looms
articles.summary: Los Angeles-based Hudson Pacific Properties reported improving office leasing activity in its Southern California portfolio, but faces a significant loan maturity in the near term that analysts are monitoring closely. The REIT's LA office properties showed increased tenant interest and deal activity compared to 2025, though the broader LA office market has plateaued in early 2026 as companies settle into return-to-office routines. Direct office vacancy for Los Angeles County has remained elevated as the market stabilizes.

articles.headline: REBNY Spotlights Creativity with 82nd Annual Most Ingenious Commercial Deal Awards
articles.summary: The Real Estate Board of New York awarded its 82nd annual Most Ingenious Commercial Deal Awards, with the first-place Henry Hart Rice Achievement Award going to Geoffrey Newman of Savills for assembling a stretch of Gramercy Park frontage over 13 years involving six buildings including a 34-unit cooperative at 252–258 Third Avenue and 37–38 Gramercy Park. The second-place Robert T. Lawrence Memorial Award went to Scott Gottlieb, Brendan Herlihy, and Michael Wellen of CBRE for a deal at 2 Penn Plaza. The competition recognizes the most creative commercial real estate transactions completed in New York City.

articles.headline: Macerich Purchases Annapolis Mall for $272 Million Including Adjacent Sears Parcel
articles.summary: Macerich has acquired Annapolis Mall in Maryland along with a 13.1-acre vacant Sears parcel adjacent to the 1.5-million-SF enclosed mall for $272 million. The mall serves the Baltimore and Washington D.C. metro areas and is anchored by Macy's, AMC Theatres, Apple, Zara, The Cheesecake Factory, Urban Outfitters, Foot Locker, Hollister, American Eagle, and Lululemon. The purchase of the adjacent Sears site provides Macerich with redevelopment optionality at one of Maryland's top retail destinations.

articles.headline: Constellation Real Estate Partners Closes on Fort Worth Land for 492,000 SF Spec Warehouse
articles.summary: Constellation Real Estate Partners has acquired 44 acres of land in Fort Worth, Texas for the development of Constellation Summit 35, a 492,000 square foot speculative industrial building. The project will be built on a speculative basis, meaning without a pre-leased tenant, targeting the active Dallas-Fort Worth industrial market. No financial terms for the land acquisition were disclosed.

articles.headline: US Industrial Vacancy Rate to Rise Into Early 2027, CoStar Revised Forecast Shows
articles.summary: CoStar's revised forecast projects the national industrial vacancy rate, currently in the mid-7% range entering Q2 2026, will edge higher into early 2027 before beginning a gradual descent. Average annual rent growth is expected to remain steady at approximately 1.0% through 2026 before reaccelerating to +2.8% by end of 2027. CoStar's national director of industrial analytics Juan Arias noted that the freight recession persisting since 2023 has primarily resulted in negative net absorption in older properties, while sublease space has begun increasing in newer properties as tenants right-size their footprints. Risks to the forecast are tilted to the downside if tariffs remain elevated or consumer spending on goods weakens.

articles.headline: Cerebras Systems IPO Set to Price as Biggest Listing of 2026
articles.summary: AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems — whose 2024 IPO attempt was derailed by a national security review — is set to price its IPO and begin trading on Thursday, positioning as the biggest stock market listing of 2026 to date. The company has secured Amazon and OpenAI as partners and calls itself the 'market leader in high-speed AI inference.' Cerebras is arriving on Wall Street amid a broader surge in semiconductor stocks, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up more than 65% in 2026. The IPO comes as investor appetite for AI infrastructure plays remains elevated.

articles.headline: Trump Heads to Beijing With Tariff Uncertainty, AI Communication, and Strait of Hormuz in Focus
articles.summary: President Trump departed for Beijing on May 12 for a summit with President Xi Jinping scheduled for May 14–15, with tariffs, AI policy, and China's role in the Iran conflict as top agenda items. The White House indicated Trump will announce new trade deals, most likely focused on agriculture, energy, and aerospace, with Boeing executives accompanying the trip and new Chinese aircraft purchases expected. The administration also plans to announce a new US-China 'board of trade' and 'board of investment' to improve communication around the AI rivalry. Top CEOs including Elon Musk of Tesla and Tim Cook of Apple are also on the trip.

articles.headline: Google Takes Space in Atlanta Industrial Property for Warehouse, Not Data Center
articles.summary: Google has leased a former Procter & Gamble warehouse in the south Atlanta region to use for storage and distribution purposes, not as a data center. The transaction signals growing corporate demand for traditional warehouse and distribution space from large technology companies expanding their physical logistics footprints. Additional details on square footage and lease terms were not disclosed publicly. The deal was reported by CoStar News on May 12, 2026.

articles.headline: Global Net Lease Strikes $535M Deal for Modiv Industrial
articles.summary: Global Net Lease agreed to acquire Modiv Industrial REIT in a $535 million deal, adding 42 industrial properties as the REIT doubles down on logistics assets. The acquisition was reported by BisNow on May 4, 2026 and GlobeSt on May 5, 2026. Modiv Industrial had been a publicly traded net-lease REIT focused on single-tenant industrial properties. The deal expands Global Net Lease's industrial footprint significantly as institutional investors continue to favor industrial/logistics as a top overweight sector.

articles.headline: Amazon Expands Into Full-Scale Third-Party Logistics Services
articles.summary: Amazon officially launched Amazon Supply Chain Services (ASCS), decoupling its logistics infrastructure from its retail marketplace to operate as a standalone service for all businesses. The platform opens Amazon's multimodal freight, automated warehousing, and last-mile parcel delivery networks to companies regardless of whether they sell on Amazon, similar to the trajectory of Amazon Web Services. Major early adopters include Procter & Gamble, 3M, and Lands' End, who are using the service to move raw materials through finished products. Amazon currently moves 13 billion items annually and is offering 96.4% on-time delivery rates, positioning ASCS as a direct competitor to traditional 3PLs and carriers like FedEx and UPS.

articles.headline: JLL: Industrial Leasing Jumped 17.8% Year-Over-Year in Q1 2026, Net Absorption Hits 50.9 MSF
articles.summary: U.S. industrial leasing activity increased 17.8% year-over-year in Q1 2026, with 145.2 million square feet of leases executed, of which 71.6% were new leases. Net absorption reached 50.9 million square feet in Q1, demonstrating exceptional strength for a historically underperforming quarter. Performance was largely driven by ongoing flight-to-quality trends and tenant consolidation into more efficient facilities. The sector maintains a cautiously optimistic outlook despite escalating geopolitical tensions, rising oil prices, and trade policy volatility.

articles.headline: Covington Group Obtains Full Entitlements for 9.4M SF Antelope Valley Commerce Center in Palmdale, CA
articles.summary: Industrial real estate specialist Covington Group obtained full entitlements for Antelope Valley Commerce Center in Palmdale, California, covering up to 9.4 million square feet on 510 acres — described as one of the largest industrial entitlements ever completed in Los Angeles County. The latest entitlements cover AVCC East at just over 8 million square feet, building on the previously approved AVCC West at approximately 1.4 million square feet. Earlier in 2026, Covington also secured a $33.8 million construction loan for a 428,185-square-foot industrial development in Hesperia, California (Inland Empire) on behalf of Pixior Group, a 3PL with an option to occupy and purchase the building. The Palmdale project is located in the northern Los Angeles County industrial corridor.

articles.headline: Port of Long Beach Commits $3.2 Billion 10-Year Capital Plan, Targeting Triple On-Dock Rail Capacity
articles.summary: New Port of Long Beach CEO Noel Hacegaba greenlit a $3.2 billion, 10-year capital spending plan — the largest of any North American port — forecasting that U.S. import volumes will continue growing faster than the overall economy despite tariff pressures. Approximately $2 billion of the investment is dedicated to rail infrastructure, with a goal of tripling on-dock rail capacity and reducing ship-to-train container transfer time from four days to 24 hours. Hacegaba and Brookfield are also exploring building what would be the world's first conventional, net-zero container terminal at the port. The port expects to double its import volume by 2050.

articles.headline: First Industrial Realty Trust Reports 41% Cash Rental Rate Increase on 2026 Leases, Tours Inland Empire Portfolio
articles.summary: First Industrial Realty Trust (NYSE: FR) reported Q1 2026 results including a 41% cash rental rate increase on leases signed to date commencing in 2026, covering 61% of 2026 expirations by square footage. The REIT successfully renewed a 556,000-square-foot facility in the Inland Empire — its largest 2026 expiration — and cash basis same-store NOI grew 8.7% in Q1. The company started two new developments in Q1 2026 totaling 305,000 square feet in Miami and Dallas with an estimated $70 million investment, and closed $425 million and $375 million unsecured term loans. First Industrial conducted an investor property tour in the Inland Empire, Southern California on May 12, 2026.

articles.headline: Q1 2026 Freight Spending Up Sharply on Tight Capacity; West Region Diesel Hit $6.60/Gallon in March
articles.summary: Total freight volumes in Q1 2026 were roughly flat quarter-over-quarter, but freight spending surged sharply as tighter capacity lifted costs through fuel surcharges and rate increases. The West region saw diesel prices hit $6.60 per gallon in late March — the highest of any EIA region — driving spending 8.5% higher quarter-over-quarter and 20.5% year-over-year despite only modest volume growth. The Midwest was the quarter's standout performer with shipments rising 5.4% sequentially and 9.5% year-over-year, though the region also saw the steepest spending surge at 19.6% sequentially. A weak used truck market limited fleet foreclosures and driver pool expansion, with ATA chief economist Bob Costello noting: 'This is a market being reshaped by supply, not demand.'

articles.headline: FreightWaves May 2026 State of the Industry: U.S. Manufacturing Returns to Expansion, Intermodal Growth Strong
articles.summary: FreightWaves' May 2026 State of the Industry white paper reports that U.S. manufacturing activity has returned to expansion, supporting flatbed, rail, and LTL demand despite broader economic mixed signals. Tight truckload conditions and attractive rate spreads are driving strong domestic intermodal growth, supported by improved service levels and available container capacity. Retail and consumer spending continue to hold up even as inflation and energy costs pressure sentiment, helping sustain freight volumes in the near term. Diesel prices remain highly sensitive to geopolitical developments — particularly the Iran conflict — complicating rate signals and reinforcing the need for cost and risk management strategies.

articles.headline: Bloomberg: Trump Tariffs on Vietnam and Southeast Asia Reshape Global Supply Chains One Year After Liberation Day
articles.summary: One year after 'Liberation Day,' Bloomberg's analysis finds that Trump's tariffs have fueled a shift in global supply chains, though not in the way the administration envisioned. China was targeted with tariffs peaking at 125%, leading to a US-China one-year truce reached in October, while China's overall trade surplus soared to record levels as it pivoted exports to markets outside the US. Universal tariffs officially sit at 10% until July 24, with threats they could rise to 15%, and the White House launched new trade investigations into 16 and 60 economies respectively, including Vietnam — now identified as a bigger tariff target due to its large US trade surplus. Foxconn and other major manufacturers continue expanding capacity in Vietnam's Bac Ninh province.

articles.headline: CRE Finance Council Q1 2026 Sentiment Index Falls 20%, Iran War Blamed for Rate Pessimism
articles.summary: The CRE Finance Council's Q1 2026 Board of Governors Sentiment Index fell 20.2% to 100.1, down from 125.4 in Q4 2025, nearly erasing three quarters of gains and returning the index to its 2017 baseline. The survey, conducted April 7–13, captured the immediate impact of the Iran conflict on rate expectations, with 61% of respondents saying the conflict would keep borrowing costs elevated by pushing out rate relief. Fifty-four percent of respondents now expect the U.S. economy to deteriorate over the next 12 months, up sharply from just 14% in Q4 2025, and 56% flagged office loans as most exposed to refinancing risk. Despite macro pessimism, 71% still expect higher borrower demand for financing and 61% expect stronger investor demand for CRE assets, suggesting repricing risk rather than a market freeze.

articles.headline: Strait of Hormuz Disruptions Force Fundamental Shift in Energy Logistics Network Design
articles.summary: Geopolitical instability in the Strait of Hormuz — which handles roughly 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas — is forcing a fundamental shift in energy logistics, moving the industry away from lowest-cost network design toward a risk-adjusted model. Repeated disruptions have transformed infrastructure planning around pipelines, storage terminals, and alternative routing, with companies building redundancy into their energy supply chains. Diesel prices have been highly sensitive to Hormuz developments, complicating freight rate signals across all transportation modes and reinforcing the need for fuel cost and risk management strategies for logistics operators. The shift is affecting both domestic U.S. energy logistics and global shipping routes serving U.S. importers.

articles.headline: S&P 500 Closes at Record 7,412.84 as Iran Ceasefire Remains Fragile; Copper Hits Record $6.46/lb
articles.summary: The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,412.84 on May 11 as markets maintained momentum following their second-best April performance since 1945. Iran sent a new ceasefire proposal to U.S. negotiators on May 11, which President Trump called 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE,' describing the month-old ceasefire as 'on life support.' Crude oil futures moved higher following the Iran developments, with oil trading above $102/barrel. Copper climbed more than 2% to a record close of $6.4605 per pound, up more than 13% year-to-date, reflecting strong industrial demand and supply concerns.
